subject: Computer Networking
title: Search Engines: Finding the Web
description: A quick, practical guide to Search Engines: Finding the Web.

hook.text: The early web had no index. Finding anything meant following links from page to page. Then search engines appeared.

buildup.text: Yahoo started as a directory — humans categorized sites by hand. AltaVista used automated crawlers instead.

discovery.text: Google launched in 1998 with PageRank — ranking pages by how many other pages linked to them. Brilliant and simple.

twist.text: Google's clean interface was mocked at first. Rivals had portals crammed with news, weather, and ads.

climax.text: By 2004, Google handled most web searches. 'Google it' became a verb in everyday language.

punchline.text: Google didn't build the web. It made it findable.

quiz.question: What algorithm made Google's search results better than competitors?
options: PageRank, which ranked pages by incoming links
An AI that read every page's content
A system where users voted on page quality

details.summary: Early search engines like AltaVista, Yahoo, and Lycos indexed the growing web. Google's PageRank algorithm, introduced in 1998, revolutionized search by ranking pages based on link authority rather than keyword matching. Search engines made the web's vast information findable.
details.whyItMatters: Without search engines, the web's information would be unfindable. Google's PageRank algorithm transformed how humanity accesses knowledge and created the dominant business model of the internet.
takeaways: Early search engines used simple keyword matching
Google's PageRank ranked pages by link authority
Search became the primary way people navigate the internet

faq.question: What made Google's approach different from earlier search engines?
faq.answer: Google treated links as votes of confidence. A page linked to by many authoritative pages was ranked higher than one with many keyword matches. This produced dramatically more relevant results and made Google the dominant search engine within a few years.

faq.question: How did search engines change the web?
faq.answer: They made it possible to find specific information among billions of pages. This created the SEO industry, defined the ad-supported business model, and made the web useful as a universal knowledge base. Search became the starting point for most internet activity.
